title: Reconfigurable field-free spin Hall nano-oscillators enabled by crystallographic anisotropy in epitaxial Co/Pt
authors: Jong-Guk Choi, Avinash Kumar Chaurasiya, Jaimin Kang, Venkatesh Vadde, Peter G. Lim, Roman Khymyn, Ahmad A. Awad, Akash Kumar, Mark C. Hersam, Vinayak P. Dravid, Pedram Khalili Amiri, Johan Åkerman
abstract: Spin Hall nano-oscillators (SHNOs) are nanoscale microwave sources for wireless communication, neuromorphic computing and oscillator-based Ising machines, but conventional devices require a global magnetic bias. Here we replace this bias through crystallographic anisotropy in epitaxial Co/Pt. Growth of hcp Co with its c-axis in the film plane produces an anisotropy field of about 0.36 T and enables field-free auto-oscillations above 10 GHz in nanoconstriction SHNOs. The active current polarity is selected by the remanent magnetization, providing nonvolatile reconfiguration of the oscillation state. Micro-focused Brillouin light scattering confirms that the nonlinear response is confined to the nanoconstriction region. Lithographic control of the angle between the current and anisotropy axes tunes the excitation threshold and drives two spectral branches from separated modes to a dominant single branch, consistent with mutual synchronization. These results establish epitaxial crystallographic anisotropy as a route to reconfigurable field-free spintronic oscillators and oscillator networks.
summary: This work reports on the creation of highly functional spin Hall nano-oscillators (SHNOs) using epitaxial Co/Pt films. By leveraging the built-in crystallographic anisotropy, the devices achieve stable, high-frequency auto-oscillations without needing an external magnetic bias. Furthermore, the oscillation state can be nonvolatilely reconfigured, establishing a promising materials-based route for next-generation spintronic oscillators.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop reconfigurable, field-free spin Hall nano-oscillators (SHNOs) to overcome the limitation of requiring a global external magnetic bias for operation.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that utilizing the intrinsic crystallographic anisotropy of epitaxial Co/Pt bilayers enables robust, field-free auto-oscillations above 10 GHz, with the oscillation state being nonvolatilely reconfigurable by the remanent magnetization.
method: The study combines advanced experimental techniques, including Spin-Torque Ferromagnetic Resonance (STFMR) and micro-focused Brillouin Light Scattering ($\mu$-BLS), with micromagnetic simulations.
model_or_system: The physical system is an epitaxial Co/Pt bilayer grown on MgO(110), patterned into nano-constrictions. The dynamics are governed by spin-torque effects interacting with the large, fixed anisotropy field derived from the crystal structure.
key_observables: Auto-oscillation frequency (>10 GHz), current-dependent microwave power spectral density, threshold current ($I_{th}$), and the degree of spectral synchronization between oscillation modes.
important_parameters: Crystallographic anisotropy field ($	ext{B}_{	ext{ani}} \approx 0.36 	ext{ T}$), current angle relative to anisotropy axis ($\phi_I$), and the operating temperature/field (zero applied field).
main_assumptions: The method relies on the assumption that the large crystallographic anisotropy is preserved after device fabrication, and that the auto-oscillation is spatially confined to the nanoconstriction region.
figures_summary: Figures show STFMR spectra confirming anisotropy fields, power spectral density demonstrating field-free auto-oscillations, and $\mu$-BLS maps illustrating the spatial confinement and the progressive merging (synchronization) of spectral branches as the current angle is tuned.
paper_structure: The paper details the experimental setup (device fabrication, measurement techniques like STFMR and $\mu$-BLS), presents the core findings regarding field-free oscillation enabled by anisotropy, and concludes by establishing this anisotropy as a general design principle for reconfigurable spintronic oscillators.
why_interesting: While the core physics is in condensed matter spintronics, the concept of using intrinsic material symmetry (crystallographic anisotropy) to engineer a stable, bias-free operating point is analogous to engineering effective Hamiltonians or potentials in quantum systems, making it relevant for understanding engineered quantum control.
